summary: 20 years later - off to the web! Step one: dragging everything we had into the new world.

changes.text: The editor moved from a Windows .exe to the browser. No install, no gzip.exe, nothing to unpack: open a save, edit, save. Your saves never leave your machine.
English is now the main language, Russian is still here. Switch it any time.
Dark and light themes, both in the spirit of good old Heroes 3.
The jokes and wisecracks of the old version moved in too.
Just drop a save onto the window.
Ctrl+O opens a file, Ctrl+S saves it.
Saving goes through the system "Save as" window: the default name gets an se_ prefix, the original stays untouched.
A warning about unsaved edits when you close the tab or open another file.
The editor figures out what wrote the save: The Shadow of Death, HD Edition or Horn of the Abyss. For HotA it warns that editing is risky.
HD Edition joins the edition list, still on a test drive.
The edition is picked from the file header, not just from the heroes.
Creature, artifact and spell lists you can search by the first letters.
Level and experience are linked: change the level and the experience follows.
Fixed old bugs nobody noticed in 20 years (well, almost nobody).
Saves with a broken gzip checksum (and Heroes writes exactly those) open without complaints.
Half-learned spells in a save no longer get lost when a hero is written back.
Presets are off to the warehouse for now, but they will be back soon.
